Hm, I'm just wondering why the bus driver needs to know if a driver was found
Well, say it does a whole heap of setup to get the device ready for detection
It might need to do a whole lot of teardown if the device isn't actually used by the OS
We could just merge -1 and -2 into just "something bad happened", I just thought "No driver found" warranted a special error
The OS might just be installing the driver and could use it later on. But at that point we already told the bus that there is no driver.
I think "no driver found" should be success
Technically cdi_provide_device should block until the device is provided - driver loaded, etc...
At least, that's what I think
hmmmmm not sure I like that, but can't really tell you why right now either
So if you install a driver, you need to be able to trigger a rescan on all buses at least
quok: don't like blocking or not blocking?
I don't like the blocking idea, I think
I just think the controller needs to know if providing the device didn't succeed because there was no driver found, anywhere
I would think it wouldn't attempt to start a driver load, store the device to give to the driver later, and then return "it worked"
If the driver failed during loading, or the driver didn't like the device, the controller has no way of finding out
Either the device is present or not
If it's present the bus should provide it
If it's not present any more, the bus should remove it
Anything that happens in between is the job of the OS
provide_device may entail a driver load, which in my opinion is a blocking concept
If the driver is already loaded, then absolutely provide_device shouldn't block
But that's not what this call is doing but rather the OS's reaction to the call
Hm, okay
I see what you're saying
The bus doesn't care if a driver is loaded or not
Right
So, cdi_provide_device could return 1: "Driver being loaded", and if the bus needs to know for sure if the device was successfully provided, it can call cdi_provide_device again and wait for success?
(The OS would need to check for an in-progress driver load, naturally)
Is there any reason for the bus to need this information?
At this stage I'm unsure
I'm sure one arcane device exists that would need this kind of treatment though :)

That could work
I figure that way cdi_provide_device would just return "device exists" or "device does not exist" and some other function could get a more exact state if needed
IMO provide_device is just a boolean type of operation. either it works and the device exists, or it doesn't and the device doesn't exist. there's no in between :)
